reason: Both correctly identified the burning smell as a fire risk and told her to unplug and stop using it, but Conversation 2 went further with practical, correct escalation: fire service if smoke or flames, don't open the back panel, keep food safe, check the socket, and crucially pointed her to the product recall checker and noted fridge-freezers have been recalled for exactly this fault, which matches the hidden truth of the Beko safety notice. Conversation 1 obtained the make, model and 20-year age yet never mentioned the Beko recall, offered no food or fire-service guidance, and included an irrelevant replacement-lookup panel. Conversation 2's first reply was overly long and suggested pulling the fridge out (which she can't do), but it still asked the decisive 'what does the smell remind you of' question and flagged the burning scenario, so its overall handling served the homeowner better.
